main_body: Wooden rack base (rows 26-46) holding three spears; two-tier open crate with shelves, drawn face-on
top_band: none — the rack base starts at an outline row 26, then a light stripe at row 27 (1px, #d59147) which is an edge highlight, not a surface; the rest is the same wood family as the front
evidence: In the column scan, the base begins with an outline at row 26 and a single 1-row highlight at row 27, followed by wood bands (rows 28-29, L=101) that belong to the front face. The base and its crossbars are flat horizontal strips seen face-on. Highlights at rows 27, 41 are 1px edge lines, not top surfaces. No beam top or base top is visible from above, so this is a front elevation with only thin rims. Spears are vertical shafts and do not count as a top. Fails the requirement that the horizontal beams and base show top faces.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 13 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 17-20 and 38-40 colours in the references. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which fits the Beodeul approach. The wood ramp has about 4 steps (dark outline, mid brown, light brown, highlight), and the spear tips have 3-4 steel tones. Surfaces are mostly plain wood bands with little grain or per-plank variation, so the piece looks thinner and flatter than the references despite having no large flat fills.
